agree.reason: The six-month severance safety net, seniority-based shift choice and the plain admission that 9-to-5 is gone give a wary teller real reasons to try the role, but the email says only 'same pay or higher' instead of the $1.50-an-hour raise, so it leaves out the strongest concrete reason to stay.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'better for everyone' claim and admits what it can't promise, but it says the phone team's 30% turnover came from 'too many calls for too few people', which no fact in the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: The 44%, 60% and 9-minute figures are passed along unchanged, and nothing is worked out from them: no severance example (10 years = 20 weeks' pay), no yearly value of the $1.50 raise (about $3,000), and no comparison of the two options in dollars.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the three-year trend that rules out keeping the branches open, but it never sets the staff member's real choice side by side, taking the role versus leaving with severance, in concrete terms.

qualification.reason: The commitments are checkable and dated (offers by Feb 14, decisions by March 1, a six-month window to leave with severance), but the open questions on training and member service have no date by which answers will come.

objections.reason: It takes on the main fears directly (phone work, rotating hours, the phone team's turnover, being stuck in a job they don't want) and doesn't raise objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of about 420 words with a clear subject line, but the signature gives only the title and leaves out Rachel Greene's name.
